title: Evacuate-First Hot-Switchover Controller for VPC Runtime Upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an "evacuate-first" upgrade controller for Private (VPC) data planes that guarantees zero-downtime runtime rollouts and fast, deterministic rollbacks. The controller prioritizes tenant session health by draining traffic from target nodes, priming caches on replacement nodes, and validating end-to-end request success before switching active routing. The feature should integrate with existing IaC (Terraform modules) and the private control plane so customers can opt into the safe rollout strategy per-tenant or per-slice.
background:
Current rolling upgrade flows sometimes surface transient tail-latency spikes and KV cache cold-start regressions for primed tenants. Existing work (see dependencies) focused on scheduling and health probes but lacks a tenant-aware evacuation-first flow that sequences
- pre-evacuation validation (synthetic probes),
- lease-based KV handoff, and
- circuit-breaker guarded traffic ceding for deterministic rollback.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can perform an evacuate-first update for a tenant slice with zero 5xx increase during the rollout (observed over a 30m canary window)
Automated priming: replacement nodes receive KV/prefix priming from drained nodes and report warm cache hit rate >= 85% before traffic shift
Rollback completes within 60s of policy-triggered abort and restores previous KV state or serves from cached snapshots
Terraform module exposes boolean flag 'evacuate_first' and relevant timeout/priming parameters; module docs and examples updated
E2E test harness (local/ci) reproduces a controlled failure and verifies circuit-breaker prevents partial switchover
design_notes: Use lease tokens (short-lived) for KV handoff to avoid dual-writer windows
Priming uses throttled background replay of recent prefixes; combined with synthetic read probes to verify warm cache
Traffic shift uses gradual session-level ceding (not connection kill) to keep long-lived sessions stable
Fallback policy: on probe failures, controller immediately reverts routing and marks node as quarantined for manual inspection
Expose telemetry: per-tenant priming progress, slot-health quorum, and rollback reason tags to Console
updates: 2026-02-12: Ticket created after infra retrospective; initial spike requested to explore lease-based handoff
2026-02-18: Spike complete — PoC shows priming reduces cold-start tail by ~72% on microbench (see linked PRs)
2026-02-25: Design review with Runtime and PM; accepted change to use session-level ceding instead of abrupt conn drain to preserve API semantics
2026-03-01: Terraform module sketch added to private-deploy IaC repo; schema includes 'evacuate_first' and priming_timeouts (PR: github.com/redwood/private-iac/pull/218)

2026-03-03: Load test (canary) against staging VPC: 10% of tenants upgraded with evacuate-first; observed no >99th percentile latency regression; one blocked shard reverted automatically — root cause: incomplete snapshot write during replacement node boot
2026-03-05: Implemented circuit-breaker thresholds and deterministic rollback path; working on runbook and operator CLI for emergency aborts
blockers: Finalizing lease token expiry semantics with storage team to ensure no data loss during handoff
E2E test flakiness in CI due to environment race; needs deterministic local harness
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Dual-write window during handoff could cause divergence — Mitigation: use lease tokens + write-forward snapshot then read-validate
Risk: Long priming times for warm-up under heavy state — Mitigation: parallelized priming with adaptive bandwidth throttling and early success thresholds
Risk: Operator confusion on rollback visibility — Mitigation: add explicit dashboard tiles and alerting with rollback reason codes
test_plan: Unit tests for lease token lifecycle and handoff logic
Integration test: deploy 5-node staging VPC, run synthetic traffic, perform evacuate-first upgrade and assert no 5xx increase and priming hit-rate >= 85%
Chaos test: kill replacement node mid-priming and assert rollback path leaves cluster in consistent state
